1.modern-en: Blind and in exile, Oedipus arrives at a sacred grove near Colonus, led by his daughter Antigone. He learns he is on ground sacred to the Eumenides and refuses to leave, declaring this place the one destined for his final rest.

2.modern-en: The local elders discover Oedipus and recoil in horror when he reveals his name. He defends himself — his crimes were done in ignorance, not malice — and calls for Theseus, king of Athens, to hear his plea.

3.modern-en: Reunited with his daughter Ismene, Oedipus learns that an oracle says his burial place will decide the fate of Thebes, and that Creon is coming to exploit him. He curses his sons for abandoning him and refuses to ever serve Thebes again.

4.modern-en: Oedipus performs a ritual of atonement at the instruction of the Chorus, sending Ismene to make the offering on his behalf. He tells the full story of his crimes — done without knowledge or malice — and argues his moral innocence.

5.modern-en: Oedipus meets Theseus and offers his body as a sacred gift to Athens: his burial place will protect the city against Thebes for all time. Theseus accepts, and Oedipus chooses to remain at the grove where his power will reside after death.

7.modern-en: Creon arrives and tries to seize Oedipus by force after failing to persuade him with words. When Creon abducts both daughters, Oedipus calls on Athens for help and hurls a bitter curse at Creon and all his line.

8.modern-en: Oedipus is defended by Theseus, who confronts Creon and forces him to lead the way to the captive girls. Oedipus again insists on his innocence before the Chorus and waits for his daughters to be restored.

9.modern-en: Oedipus is joyfully reunited with his daughters and thanks Theseus warmly. He refuses to hear his son Polyneices but relents under pressure from Antigone and Theseus, and delivers a devastating final curse on both his sons.

10.modern-en: Thunder and lightning signal that the hour of his death is at hand. Oedipus sends urgently for Theseus, determined to fulfill his promise to Athens before he dies.

11.modern-en: Oedipus leads Theseus alone to the secret place of his death, passing from life by a mysterious and painless divine summons. His hidden grave becomes a sacred, unseen source of power protecting Athens forever.

1.modern-en: Antigone guides her blind father on his wanderings, helping him find the sacred grove at Colonus and negotiate with the local stranger. She is his eyes and his constant companion.

2.modern-en: When the Chorus threatens to expel Oedipus, Antigone pleads on his behalf, urging mercy for a man whose crimes were done without intent. She steadies her father through the frightening confrontation with the elders.

3.modern-en: Antigone witnesses the reunion with Ismene and hears the oracle's news about Oedipus's grave. She stands by her father as he curses his absent sons and processes the weight of the new prophecy.

4.modern-en: When Oedipus is too weak to perform the ritual of atonement himself, Antigone agrees to carry it out alongside Ismene.

7.modern-en: Creon's guards seize Antigone by force, tearing her away from her father while she cries out for help. She is taken as Creon's hostage, leaving Oedipus without his guide.

9.modern-en: Rescued by Theseus, Antigone is joyfully reunited with her father. She then pleads with Oedipus to hear Polyneices, arguing that even a painful meeting could do no lasting harm — showing her instinct for reconciliation even in impossible circumstances.

10.modern-en: Antigone stands beside her father as the thunder sounds. She asks what solemn charge he intends to lay on Theseus, sensing the end is near.

11.modern-en: After Oedipus's mysterious death, Antigone mourns deeply and longs to see the hidden tomb. Refused by Theseus on her father's orders, she resolves with Ismene to return to Thebes and try to prevent their brothers from destroying each other.

2.modern-en: Antigone spots a lone rider approaching and recognizes her sister Ismene, who has traveled far alone to find them.

3.modern-en: Ismene arrives with urgent news: an oracle declares that Oedipus's burial place will determine Thebes's fate, and Creon is on his way to use Oedipus as a political pawn. She has risked the dangerous journey out of loyalty to her father.

4.modern-en: Ismene volunteers to perform the ritual libation on her father's behalf so that Oedipus need not move from the sacred ground, then goes off to carry it out.

7.modern-en: Ismene is mentioned as already seized by Creon's men even before Antigone is taken — Creon has stripped Oedipus of both daughters at once.

9.modern-en: Ismene is returned to her father alongside Antigone by Theseus and his men. She is present at the reunion and for the agonizing interview with Polyneices.

11.modern-en: After Oedipus's death, Ismene mourns alongside Antigone and despairs at the thought of living on alone and friendless. The sisters decide together to return to Thebes.

1.modern-en: Theseus is named by the local stranger as the king of Athens — the man Oedipus immediately asks to summon, sensing that a meeting with the ruler of Athens is the key to his fate.

4.modern-en: The Chorus announces that Theseus is approaching, summoned by news of Oedipus's famous and terrible name.

5.modern-en: Theseus meets Oedipus with generous respect, immediately grasps the importance of his offer, and grants him Athenian protection and citizenship. He promises no one will remove Oedipus by force, and his word alone is enough — no oath needed.

7.modern-en: Called away from a sacrifice at Poseidon's altar, Theseus rushes back to find that Creon has seized the daughters. He instantly orders cavalry and infantry to cut off the abductors before they can cross the border.

8.modern-en: Theseus confronts Creon directly, rebukes him for shaming both Athens and Thebes with his lawless act, and forces him to lead the way to where the daughters are held.

9.modern-en: Theseus returns with the rescued daughters and receives Oedipus's heartfelt thanks. When told Polyneices is at Poseidon's altar as a suppliant, he urges Oedipus to hear him out of reverence for the god — and will not take no for an answer.

10.modern-en: Urgently summoned as the thunder signs multiply, Theseus hurries back to be with Oedipus at the end. He is the one person Oedipus trusts with the final secret.

11.modern-en: Theseus receives the secret location of Oedipus's death-place — a hidden gift that will protect Athens against its enemies forever. After the miraculous passing, he comforts the daughters and gently refuses to let them see the tomb, honoring Oedipus's last command.

3.modern-en: Ismene warns Oedipus that Creon is on his way to Colonus — not to honor him but to keep him near the Theban border under Theban control, exploiting the oracle that ties Oedipus's burial place to Thebes's security.

7.modern-en: Creon arrives with armed attendants and tries smooth words first, then force. When persuasion fails, he has both daughters seized as hostages and threatens to seize Oedipus himself, provoking the Chorus and a confrontation with the Athenian state.

8.modern-en: Creon is challenged by Theseus and tries to justify the abductions as lawful. Overruled and humiliated, he is forced to lead Theseus to where the girls are held, and leaves under escort with a veiled threat of future reprisals from Thebes.

3.modern-en: Oedipus condemns both his sons for abandoning him. Ismene reveals that Polyneices and his brother Eteocles are locked in a deadly power struggle over Thebes, each knowing that their father's blessing could decide the outcome.

9.modern-en: Polyneices arrives weeping, acknowledging he failed his father, and asks for Oedipus's blessing before marching on Thebes with his Argive allies. Oedipus refuses savagely and curses both sons to kill each other in battle. Polyneices accepts his doom but cannot turn back without losing face — he asks his sisters to give him proper burial when the time comes.
